summary: Give the reading assistant the whole paper and a vision path. On reader open the browser extracts each page's text with pdf.js into a cached fulltext table; questions now retrieve the most relevant passages locally (8, or 14 with 更多上下文) with page labels instead of only the abstract. Figure/table questions trigger a local caption search, render the matching page to a JPEG and call the new paper_vision_qa operation through the same gateway (deepseek-flash serves vision, so it is a payload-mode switch, not a model switch). Modes are labelled on every answer.
scope_note: Covers the diff since commit 13215c1. Adds a fulltext table, a new registered operation + prompt contract + source entry, and UI extraction/vision wiring; one real vision call and several text calls were made.

budget_impact.rationale: New registered operation paper_vision_qa (cap 8,000 in / 1,100 out) and a vision_qa_starter scenario. Existing ceilings were not changed. One real vision call cost $0.00102 (2,839 tokens, 1x1 test image); text questions use the existing paper_qa ceiling.
budget_impact.before: QA could only use title + abstract; one text operation.
budget_impact.after: QA uses cached full text plus an optional one-page image; vision has its own operation, envelope and prompt contract.
budget_impact.period: one vision call plus text calls on 2026-09-11

additional_checks.scope: 25 pages / 72,200 chars cached; 7 passages retrieved; answer correctly reported the paper has no Figure 2

reviews.reviewer: Implementing agent; feature work, not recommendation quality

open_risks: Vision quality on a real rendered figure is unverified (tested with a 1x1 image to prove the request shape and cost path).
Image token cost is an estimate (~1,500/page); a dense page may cost more.
Extraction runs in the background after the reader opens; a question asked too early falls back to the abstract.
Lexical retrieval can miss a passage whose wording differs from the question.
Recommendation quality remains unproven; gates stay not_run.
